question: Who are the securities in the 'ipo<=2021_or_unknown' tail bucket of the first-appearance cross-reference (F3 n=7, F4 n=8)? Are they genuine old IPOs admitted at a multi-year lag, or universe re-entries (long suspension / restructuring / code change)?
method: tushare stock_basic MCP, fields ts_code+name+list_date+delist_date, one call per code, 2026-09-16; all 15 tail-bucket codes of F3 and F4 resolved (F1 n=468 and F2 n=112 tails NOT resolved, see not_done).

cohort_identity_check.note: Securities first appearing in the panel, grouped by IPO cohort, summed across folds.

cohort_2022.caveat: lag-4/lag-5 admissions are demonstrably non-zero (the F4 tail bucket is 8 such securities from the 2020-2021 cohorts), so a handful of 2022-cohort securities could still first appear in 2026+, which the frozen panel cannot observe. The exact 335=335 match is therefore consistent with complete absorption by lag 3 but does not prove it.

cohort_2023.caveat: lag3 lands in 2026+, outside the panel.

cohort_2024.caveat: lag2+ lands in 2026+, outside the panel. This is why F4's largest tranche is only 63.

cohort_2025.caveat: zero same-year admission in every fold; the entire 2025 cohort is outside the panel. This refutes reading F4's 109 as 'the 2025 IPO class'.

lag2_rate_stability.reading: the lag-2 admission rate is 14.0% and 13.9% on the two cohorts where it is observable, i.e. the lag kernel is stable and not a per-fold artifact.

not_done: F1's tail bucket (n=468, the whole fold) and F2's (n=112) were NOT resolved code by code; only F3 (7) and F4 (8) were, because those two are fully enumerated and small.
No exact 2021 non-BSE IPO cohort count was derived: a new_share query for 2021 H1 succeeded on retry but the response was truncated in transit, so F1's 468 is not decomposed into cohort tranches.
The exact upstream rule producing the hard zero on same-year admission was not introspected (universe_daily construction is read-only and was not queried).
